business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ownership and Cross-Border Sub-Licensing of Trademarks and Patents

stage_1.expense_line_item: Company name pre-clearance / advance ruling (Firmenvorbescheid) with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht/CO), Art. 620-640 (formation and registration of Aktiengesellschaft), Art. 626 (mandatory articles), Art. 629-632 (share capital and payment-in requirement), Art. 643 (commercial register application)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Canton of Zug Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt Zug), subordinate to the Federal Commercial Register Office (HReg) for supervisory oversight
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) and signed Commercial Register application form (Handelsregisteranmeldung), filed under Art. 640 CO
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value of each registered share, and in all cases at least CHF 50,000, must be paid into a Swiss bank blocked escrow account in the company's name before the Commercial Register entry is confirmed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Board of Directors hereby acknowledges the incorporation of CH_AG, adopts the Articles of Association, ratifies the subscription of all registered shares, and confirms the minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 has been irrevocably paid into the blocked Swiss bank escrow account, with at least CHF 50,000 available to the company. The registered office established in the Canton of Zug is adopted. The Board appoints [Director A] and [Director B] as board members, [Name] as Chair, [Name] as Registered Agent, and [Name] as Compliance Officer, and authorises the Chair and Registered Agent to execute the Commercial Register application and corporate governance documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and notarise articles of association and deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public licensed in Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the German-language Articles of Association in standard AG form, specifying the name CH_AG, registered office in Zug, purpose limited to ownership and global sub-licensing of patents and trademarks, share capital CHF 100,000 divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 each. Appear before a Zug notary with the drafted deed; the notary will verify the name against the Commercial Register and formally notarise the deed and articles.
required_dossiers: Name search result/no-objection in the Commercial Register
Passports or valid ID of incorporators
Power of attorney if executed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a name collision or formal defect, amend the articles and re-notarise; the notary will submit a fresh name-availability query. Supplemental notary fees may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked share-capital account and deposit paid-in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-supervised Swiss bank maintaining a blocked account in the company's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarised deed of incorporation to the bank and open a blocked business account in the name of 'CH_AG i.G.'. Each incorporator pays their subscribed portion by wire transfer from a disclosed bank account. A minimum aggregate of CHF 100,000 must be credited, with at least CHF 50,000 remaining freed for business purposes after the blocking release. The bank issues the statutory capital-deposit confirmation certifying that the funds are irrevocably at the company's disposal.
required_dossiers: Authenticated list of subscribers and payments
Beneficial owner declaration and underlying identification
Bank account opening forms and banking KYC package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the blocked-account confirmation is delayed, obtain an interim bank statement showing final credit and request expedited confirmation. If the bank demands additional source-of-funds evidence, supply sworn asset declarations and remittance records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit commercial register application with supporting corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canton of Zug Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt Zug), using the secure Swiss Commercial Register filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Commercial Register application in the official form, certifying the organ appointments and paid-up capital. Attach the notarised deed, articles, bank capital-deposit certificate, consent to act of each legal representative, and specimen signatures. The registry will examine compliance with the Swiss Code of Obligations and enter CH_AG in the Commercial Register; the entry is then published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Written consent forms and specimen signatures of directors and authorised signatories
Passport copies and extract of beneficial owners for non-resident officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a formal objection (e.g. missing proof of capital or incomplete director data), cure the defect by filing the requested corrected instrument within the statutory period. In complex queries, request a preliminary conference and a ruling that preserves the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene the first board meeting and adopt corporate governance resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial board meeting (physically or by circular resolution) immediately after Commercial Register entry. Ratify the share subscription and registered office, formally elect the Chairman, delegate signature authority, appoint a secretary and a registered agent, and approve an organisational regulation covering IP licensing policies, transfer-pricing documentation, and corporate treasury controls. Record the meeting in minutes signed by the chairman and minute-taker.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting and agenda
Consent to act and signature authority forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable to attend, use a written unanimous circular resolution signed by all board members. If the articles require a notarised board resolution, hold a formal meeting before a notary and file the notarial transcript.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with federal tax, value-added tax, and social insurance authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for UID/VAT, together with the Canton Zug Compensation Office (AHV Ausgleichskasse) and Suva for social insurance enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Commercial Register entry, the UID reference number is automatically issued by the Federal Statistical Office. File the VAT registration with ESTV if annual worldwide turnover from licensing royalties exceeds CHF 100,000, or elect VAT voluntarily if appropriate. Register the company and its employees with the AHV compensation office for old-age/survivors' insurance contributions, and submit an employer registration to Suva for statutory accident insurance coverage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ESTV queries the substance of the Swiss entity or the VAT registration is suspended, submit a letter explaining actual management of IP licensing, contracts, and royalty flows in Switzerland. If AHV registration is referred to the residence canton, provide the commercial register excerpt proving the Zug registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial authority competent for passive intellectual-property holding and licensing; any ancillary office activity in Zug remains subject only to the Cantonal Economic and Labour Board for generic occupational safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing license required under ISIC 6420 (patent/trademark ownership and cross-border licensing); non-mandatory confirmation letter may be issued by Zug Commercial Register.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU), acting through the Canton of Zug Environmental Protection Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal environmental impact assessment because the activity is intangible IP licensing without construction, production facility, or physical installation under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV) Annex 1.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or waste streams arise from patent licensing. If limited office use occurs, the general duty of care under the Federal Water Protection Act (GSchG Art. 6) and the General Air Pollution Control Ordinance (LRV Art. 3) applies, and the waste-handling reporting duty is limited to ordinary administrative waste disposal by the municipality.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for the licensed activity itself. For any rented office space, the employer must notify Suva/Swiss accident insurance, comply with EKAS workplace guidelines (health and safety), and maintain locally required fire-safety signage and an emergency concept. Canton Zug building inspectorate approval applies only to structural alterations, not to normal office use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA; Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC) for federal direct tax, withholding tax and VAT; cantonal tax administrations (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) for cantonal and communal taxes. Official portals: www.estv.admin.ch, www.uid.admin.ch (UID register) and the FTA VAT e-service portal ('Mein Konto').
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The AG is entered in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister) and automatically obtains the unified business identifier (UID, Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), which serves as the statutory tax number, VAT ID and invoicing identifier for all federal and cantonal taxes. VAT registration is filed with the FTA through the VAT e-portal once taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or for voluntary registration; the FTA confirms the taxpayer registration and the 'MWST' suffix is appended to the UID for VAT purposes. Foreign entities with Swiss VAT liability register directly with the FTA; non-resident licensors may alternatively rely on the reverse-charge procedure when the Swiss recipient is liable. Formation of the AG requires a licensed revision office (Prüfstelle) and notarized statutes; no physical Swiss office is required, but a Swiss correspondence address and authorized representative are expected for registration and tax correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Swiss AG is a resident corporate taxpayer liable on worldwide income (Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax, DBG), with foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate exempt with progression under relevant treaty and domestic rules; no pass-through treatment is available for a stock company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law has no US-style check-the-box election and no general hybrid mismatch election, but provides specific statutory elections: (1) patent/IP-box election granting up to 90% reduction of net qualifying IP royalty income at federal and cantonal level (STAF 2020 regime, Art. 24b DBG); (2) notional interest deduction (NID) election in cantons that enacted it, reducing excessive equity taxation on intra-group financing; (3) VAT group election for Swiss related parties; (4) opt-in to tax real estate supplies to preserve input VAT recovery; (5) tax-neutral restructuring and merger election for licensed carry-over of assets and tax attributes; (6) participation relief on intercompany royalty/dividend income is automatic, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Swiss federal value added tax; Mehrwertsteuer MWST / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée TVA / Imposta sul valore aggiunto IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual gross turnover from taxable supplies (Art. 10 para. 2 let. a MWSTG). Foreign businesses without a Swiss seat must register if their Swiss taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; voluntary registration below the threshold is permitted. Outbound B2B IP licensing to non-resident licensees falls outside Swiss VAT scope, so such royalty income alone does not trigger Swiss VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based e-invoicing. The Swiss QR-Invoice (QR-Rechnung) is mandatory on payment slips issued to Swiss payers since 30 June 2020; structured e-invoicing (eBill, XML, EDI) is accepted with fully auditable electronic archiving. All VAT-relevant invoices must be retained for 10 years (Art. 58 MWSTG) and produced to the FTA on request; no government pre-clearance or fiscal stamping exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: the 0% rate applies when ownership in movable goods is transferred to an acquirer abroad and the goods are physically exported, evidenced by a valid customs export declaration and transport documents. Services: cross-border patent/trademark licensing and sub-licensing is governed by the B2B place-of-receipt rule (Art. 8 MWSTG); where the licensee has its seat or permanent establishment abroad and is a taxable person, the income is not subject to Swiss VAT, may be invoiced at 0%, and the licensor retains full input VAT recovery. Services performed directly in connection with exported goods are zero-rated as ancillary export services. The AG must maintain the full licensing contract identifying the registered patents/trademarks, the royalty calculation, the foreign licensee seat and the licensee's valid foreign VAT/UID number.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certified customs export declaration (Ausfuhrzolldeklaration) containing the official export number and release stamp of the Federal Office of Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing the physical export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / bank credit advice proving receipt of the royalty from abroad within the repatriation window
License/sub-license agreement with complete IP identification, royalty formula and foreign licensee seat
Commercial invoice and Swiss QR-invoice (QR-Rechnung) issued with an explicit 0% VAT statement
Certificate of seat/residence and valid foreign VAT identification number of the licensee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA rigorously audits export substantiation: if the export is not proven within the statutory deadlines, the supply is reclassified as domestic turnover subject to VAT at 8.1% (or the applicable reduced/special rate), input VAT deductions are clawed back, and default interest at 5% p.a. accrues. Administrative fines reach up to three times the tax evaded for intentional violation (Art. 64 MWSTG) and up to ten times for fraudulent evasion; criminal prosecution under Swiss criminal and customs law may lead to imprisonment. The assessment limitation period is 10 years for tax evasion and 5 years in ordinary cases, with retrospective adjustment of zero-rated credits and refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) – Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca Nazionale Svizzera, within the framework of the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for financial market policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility of the Swiss franc (CHF) for both current and capital transactions and has accepted the obligations of Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no foreign exchange controls, no mandatory Central Bank approvals for cross-border payments, and no restriction on conversion of licensee or shareholder payments. Profit remittance, royalty distribution, capital inflows and outflows are freely transferable subject only to ordinary bank compliance screening, anti-money-laundering law, sanctions filters, and the Swiss federal withholding tax framework applicable to dividend distributions only; royalty payments are not subject to Swiss withholding tax. Tax and transfer-pricing substance must still be demonstrable to convert economically genuine licensing income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no mandatory surrender, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no compelled conversion ratio for export receipts or foreign-currency proceeds. A Swiss IP holding company may lawfully retain foreign currency balances, convert or deploy them at will through licensed banks, provided its accounting system documents the underlying licensing agreements and arm's-length consideration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Receivables Collection Account
Operational Account, domestic clearing rail alternative

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-low for primary treasury reliance. Swiss FINMA-licensed neobanks or FinTech companies acting under the FinTech Banking Licence (deposit-taking up to CHF 100 million but no interest business) may hold payment accounts, but they do not provide the full international treasury, FX derivative, custody and correspondent banking depth of a Tier-1 commercial bank. Offshore digital EMI accounts, particularly EU/UK E-Money Institution wallets, are not recognized as local bank equivalents for intercompany royalty inflows in a Swiss AG IP HoldCo and may trigger bank responsibility concerns, tax attribution obstacles, and inadequate AML-governance standards; acceptance depends on the specific counterparty's FINMA authorisation and the bank relationship of the Swiss entity. Accordingly, they should be used only as ancillary disbursement channels, not as the principal inbound royalty clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Aktiengesellschaft with foreign ownership and an IP-holding business profile, Swiss banks under FINMA AMLA rules generally require at least one physical attestation and a personal or video-identification interview of the ultimate beneficial owner together with the signatories. Digital remote on-boarding is permitted if the bank applies FINMA-compliant audiovisual identification and enhanced due diligence, but many Tier-1 and cantonal banks will nevertheless require one director or a senior officer with power of attorney to appear at the registered Swiss agent or branch before account activation. Practical recommendation: the ultimate beneficial owner should plan for at least one physical presence in Zurich or Geneva for final compliance interview and signature certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign legal-entity ownership with intermediate holding companies or trust-like layers triggering UBO opacity concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Swiss commercial-register excerpt, unaudited or audited corporate chart, up-to-date share register showing all registered shareholders, UBO declaration for every ownership layer above 25%, passport copies, residence proof, resolution of the board of directors designating authorised signatories, and a clearly documented source-of-funds statement for initial capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty flows to or from related parties in preferential-tax or low-transparency jurisdictions, creating transfer-pricing and money-velocity concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed patent licensing or sub-licensing agreements, ownership chain for the licensed patents and trademarks, Swiss tax ruling or private ruling application covering the AG's activities, OECD master file / local file, intercompany transfer-pricing study using TNMM or CUP method, and a commercial substance file evidencing actual management decisions in Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential PEP status or adverse media exposure of the ultimate beneficial owner, shareholder vehicles, or foreign licensee-network companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP questionnaire, professional and domestic-source-of-wealth letters, adverse-media search result, sanctions-list screening report, independent legal opinion on beneficial ownership, and contemporaneous board minutes confirming the validation and rationale of each cross-border royalty arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of bearer-share holdings or nominee shareholding arrangements in the company history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of conversion to strictly registered shares under the Swiss Code of Obligations, share register disclosing ultimate holders, certified statements from any former nominee, and notarised minutes of the extraordinary shareholders' meeting approving the share-realignment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: CHF capital contributions from shareholders or intermediate holding companies enter Switzerland freely without SNB or SIF approval. Equity capital contributions must be labelled as such with the instruction narrative 'Equity contribution' and a stabilised purpose code, normally 'INTC' (Intercompany Payment) or 'ROYL' if routed as a license-funding royalty, as defined by the corresponding bank's SWIFT purpose-code matrix. Shareholder loans should be received under a written shareholder-loan agreement, with interest rate and repayment schedule aligned with Swiss transfer-pricing rules and OECD standards, and the remitting bank must complete standard bank-form declarations showing commercial origin. Authorised Swiss bank accounts require no exchange-control permit, but documentation inside the bank account opening file must support the source of funds, ownership chain, and the development-stage capital requirement of the AG.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the Swiss IP treasury rely on SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) as the primary rail for royalty payments to foreign licensees or upstream patent holders, with MT202 COV used only for bank-to-bank correspondent clearing. Domestic CHF settlements route through Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC/SIC4) or SIX Telekurs channels; EUR-denominated workflow runs through the TARGET2 / T2 system and SEPA Credit Transfers as permitted. Where a patent licensee requires payment against acceptance or instalment milestones, the confirming bank may issue a SWIFT MT700 documentary / commercial letter of credit or MT760 standby letter of credit as performance security; all outbound wires must include full transaction purpose and payment narrative in English, and any royalty transfer must cite the underlying licence agreement and, where applicable, the invoice or royalty statement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Bilateral OTC FX forwards with UBS, ZKB, BCV or another bank counterparty, transacted under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and a standard Swiss CSA for collateralisation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with exceptional capital controls or limited SWIFT-clearing availability, to hedge projected royalty receipts from restricted jurisdictions
Cross-currency swaps (FX swap and long-term cross-currency interest-rate swaps) to manage duration and principal exposure of foreign-currency licence receivables
Vanilla FX options, zero-collared tunnels, and participating forwards to maintain budget-rate certainty while preserving SME treasury flexibility under banks' existing FX-derivative credit lines
Collateralised rolling spot-forward structures limited to genuine trade and royalty-transaction exposure, consistent with the AG's hedging policy and FINMA/AIFM conduct expectations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return together with audited or unaudited annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end; extensions commonly granted to 30 September on canton-specific timelines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on taxes found due at 4.5% per annum; late-filing procedural fines up to CHF 10,000; risk of official assessment (Ermessenseinschätzung)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT periodical or annual return if annual taxable supplies exceed CHF 100,000; cross-border royalty income generally subject to Swiss VAT or reverse-charge rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration – VAT Division (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the close of each VAT period; annual filers generally due by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge up to 5% of tax due; default interest at 4.5% per annum; summary penalties for VAT evasion up to CHF 20,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required if the AG exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million net turnover, or 250 full-time employees on annual average; also mandatory for listed companies or upon shareholder request where shareholders holding at least 10% of share capital so demand
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (arts. 958–963); Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS permitted for non-listed companies; statutory accounts prepared in Swiss francs (CHF)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing to the commercial register. Non-listed AGs must maintain a Beneficial Owner Register (Art. 697j ff. CO) and identify any shareholder holding at least 25% of shares or voting rights, as well as any controlling natural person. The shareholder register (Aktienregister) must be updated upon each share transfer; director changes and other register mutations are filed to the Commercial Register when they occur, not on an annual schedule

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – 2,500 per annum for Swiss registered office and corporate services agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 18,000 for a limited audit; USD 20,000 – 80,000 for an ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal direct profit tax imposed on profit after taxes, economically equivalent to 7.83% of the pre-federal-tax base; combined federal-cantonal-communal statutory headline for a Zug-domiciled Aktiengesellschaft: approximately 11.9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: TRAF 2020 patent box regime: the Canton of Zug exempts 90% of qualifying net patent-licensing income from cantonal/communal profit tax, requiring qualifying Swiss R&D activity; combined effective rate on Swiss-qualified patent royalty streams falls to approximately 8.2-9.5%. Participation deduction: qualifying participations of at least 10% held on a durable basis produce 100% federal and cantonal exemption of dividend and capital-gain income. R&D super-deduction: additional deduction of up to 50% of qualifying Swiss R&D expenditure, fully implemented in Zug. Legacy privileged statuses A/B/C have been abolished; no harmful preferential regimes remain.
